flagged.evidence: The title says “Skein-module isomorphisms preserve framings and boundary actions.” The Statement proves framing transport for isomorphisms induced by orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms, and boundary-action intertwining only when specified collars are carried productwise. The title omits these restrictions and reads more broadly than the result.

The cited general-position supplier requires “both end projections under the fixed π” to be regular. Proof 5.1 chooses S³ endpoint diagrams using Step 3.2, which gives regular projections for links individually but does not specify one common projection direction for both endpoints. The regular-projection lemma’s proof excludes only null sets of directions, so a common direction exists; stating this choice would close the local gap.
